spec: Bucket each non-negative integer age into a decade label: '0-9', '10-19', ..., '90-99', or '100+' for ages 100 and above. Return a dict mapping each label that has at least one age to the count of ages in it (labels with no ages are omitted). An empty list returns an empty dict.

Split text on whitespace and count how often each adjacent pair of words (a bigram) occurs, using a single space to join the pair into a key like 'word1 word2'. Return a dict mapping each bigram string to its count. A text with fewer than two words returns an empty dict.
visible_tests: assert count_bigrams('the cat sat') == {'the cat': 1, 'cat sat': 1}
counter_input: assert count_bigrams('m n o m n') == {'m n': 2, 'n o': 1, 'o m': 1}

spec: Write a function that returns the k largest values from a list, sorted in descending order, including duplicates. If k is greater than or equal to the length of the list, return all elements sorted descending. If k is 0, return an empty list.

Validate a credit-card-style string of the format 'XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX' where each X is a digit: exactly four groups of four digits separated by hyphens. Additionally the 16 digits (read without hyphens) must pass the Luhn checksum (double every second digit from the right, subtracting 9 if over 9, and the total must be divisible by 10). Return True only if both the format and the checksum are valid.
Given a non-empty list of rows, where each row is a list of integers, compute the sum of each row, then return the median (as a float, using the odd/even averaging rule) of those row sums.
Determine whether a positive integer n is an emirp: n is prime, its decimal digit-reversal is also prime, and the reversal is a different number from n.

Write a function that returns the length of the longest common suffix shared by two lists, i.e. the number of trailing positions at which the two lists have equal elements before the first mismatch (scanning from the end), or before either list is exhausted. Either list may be empty, giving a result of 0.
Determine whether a non-negative integer n is trimorphic: the decimal representation of n cubed ends with the decimal representation of n.

Validate a string of simplified tags where each tag is either a matched pair opening '<word>' ... closing '</word>' (word is one or more lowercase letters, properly nested) or a self-closing tag '<word/>'. No other text is allowed anywhere. Return True if the whole string decomposes into such tags with correct nesting; otherwise return False.

Given a list of items and a dictionary mapping some items to integer ranks, sort the items ascending by their rank. Items not present in the dictionary are placed after all ranked items, and ties (including among unranked items) preserve their original relative order from the input.
submission:
def sort_by_custom_rank_map(items, rank_map):
    default_rank = len(items) + 1000
    indexed = list(enumerate(items))
    indexed.sort(key=lambda pair: (rank_map.get(pair[1], default_rank), pair[0]))
    return [item for _, item in indexed]

spec: Format an integer as a string with commas separating groups of three digits, keeping a leading minus sign for negative numbers in front of the separated digits.

Given a list of integers and an integer k, return the k most frequent distinct values as a list, most frequent first. Values with equal frequency are ordered with the smaller value first. If there are fewer than k distinct values, return all of them; k is always non-negative.
submission:
def top_k_frequent_values(items, k):
    from collections import Counter
    freq = Counter(items)
    ordered = sorted(set(items), key=lambda v: (-freq[v], v))
    return ordered[:k]

spec: Given a list of strings each formatted as 'key<sep>value' (splitting only on the first occurrence of sep so the value may itself contain sep), parse them into a dict. If the same key appears more than once, keep the value from its last occurrence. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a start and end integer day number (start <= end) and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) treated as non-business days, return the count of non-business days in the inclusive range [start, end].

Write a function that groups the elements of a list of integers into a dictionary keyed by their remainder modulo a given positive integer n, where each key maps to the list of elements with that remainder in their original relative order, and keys with no matching elements are omitted. The input list may be empty.
Determine whether the decimal digits of the absolute value of an integer n are in strictly increasing order from left to right. A single-digit number is trivially strictly increasing.

Return a new list containing the elements of the input list with duplicates removed, keeping only the first occurrence of each distinct value and preserving the original relative order. Elements are compared with equality.

Write a function that finds the maximum product obtainable by multiplying two distinct-position elements from a list of numbers (the list may contain negative numbers, so the best pair might be the two largest or the two most negative values). Assume the list has at least two elements.
Determine whether a positive integer n is an emirp: n is prime, its decimal digit-reversal is also prime, and the reversal is a different number from n.

Write a function that returns the sum of each contiguous window of length k from a list, in order, as a list of numbers. If k is not a positive integer at most the length of the list, return an empty list.
Parse a hexadecimal string s (digits 0-9 and letters a-f, case-insensitive, no sign) into its equivalent non-negative decimal integer value.
Compute the sum of the distinct prime factors of an integer n >= 2.
Compute the sum of all positive divisors of a positive integer n, including 1 and n itself.

Mask the local part of an email address (the part before the '@'): keep the first and last character visible and replace every character in between with '*', keeping the domain part unchanged. If the local part is only one character, leave it as-is; if it is two characters, mask the second with '*'.

Count the number of maximal contiguous runs of vowel characters (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) in a string, where a run is one or more consecutive vowels bounded by non-vowel characters or the ends of the string.

Write a function that rearranges a list of integers so that all even numbers come first, followed by all odd numbers, with each group preserving its original relative order from the input list. Return an empty list for an empty input.
Given a dict mapping keys to non-empty lists of numbers, compute the range (max minus min) of each list. Return a dict mapping each key to that range. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Validate a checksum string of digits where the last digit is a check digit for the ones before it. Assign alternating weights +1, -1, +1, -1, ... (by position from the left, starting at +1) to the digits before the check digit, sum the signed values, and the check digit must equal that sum modulo 10 (Python's modulo, always non-negative). The body (all but the last character) must be non-empty and contain only digits. Return False otherwise.
Given a string s, return a copy of s with every character that is not an alphabetic letter removed, preserving the order and original case of the remaining letters.
Wrap the given string with a leading left curly double-quote character (“) and a trailing right curly double-quote character (”), with no other changes to the string's contents.
visible_tests: assert smart_quotes('a quote inside " here') == '“a quote inside " here”'

spec: Write a function that finds the second largest distinct value in a list of numbers (duplicates of the largest value do not count as separate values). Return None if the list has fewer than two distinct values.

Given cells and matching widths, force each cell to exactly its column width: if the cell is longer than the width, cut it down to the first width characters; if it is shorter, left-justify it with trailing spaces. Join the resulting fixed-width columns with a single space.

Validate whether the single-quote characters (') in a string s are properly paired. Scanning left to right, each ' toggles between an outside-quotes and inside-quotes state, starting outside. Return True if the string ends in the outside-quotes state, meaning there is an even number of ' characters in total; otherwise return False. All other characters are irrelevant.

Validate a grid reference string consisting of a single uppercase letter followed by digits representing an integer from 1 to 99 with no leading zero (e.g. 'A1', 'B23', 'Z99'). Return False otherwise.

Split the list into consecutive chunks of size n, each returned as its own list, preserving the original order of elements. The final chunk may contain fewer than n elements if the list length is not evenly divisible by n. Assume n is a positive integer. An empty list returns an empty list of chunks.
Count how many keys in d equal their own mapped value (a 'fixed point', e.g. {'a': 'a'}). Return that count as an integer. An empty dict, or one with no such keys, returns 0.

Given a string s, split it into a list of maximal runs of consecutive characters that are either all letters or all digits, preserving order. Any character that is neither a letter nor a digit acts only as a separator (it never appears in the output) and always forces a break, even between an adjacent letter run and digit run.
Join a list of lowercase words into a single PascalCase string by capitalizing each word and concatenating them with no separators. An empty list returns an empty string.
Interleave two strings character by character, alternating starting with the first string, and appending any leftover characters from the longer string at the end once the shorter one is exhausted.
Count how many prime numbers lie in the inclusive integer range [a, b], where 0 <= a <= b.
